proposals.before: Tian Ying, Qi Wei King young son and Qi Xuan King concubine brother.
proposals.after: Tian Ying was Qi Wei King's youngest son and Qi Xuan King's younger half-brother.
proposals.reason: 庶弟 means younger paternal half-brother, not 'concubine brother'; 少子 is youngest son.

proposals.before: His mother secretly raise give birth.
proposals.after: His mother secretly raised him and kept him alive.
proposals.reason: 舉生之 means raised him so that he lived, not 'give birth'; the English is also ungrammatical.

proposals.before: Tian Ying angrily berated his mother: 'I commanded you to abandon this child, yet you dared to give birth to him. Why?'
proposals.after: Tian Ying angrily berated his mother: 'I commanded you to abandon this child, yet you dared to raise him. Why?'
proposals.reason: In context 生之 continues 舉/勿舉 and means keep alive/raise, not give birth; the birth already occurred.

proposals.before: Tian Ying angry his mother: My command you abandon this child, dare give birth, why?
proposals.after: Tian Ying angry at his mother: I commanded you to abandon this child, yet you dared to raise him; why?
proposals.reason: Same 生之 error as in the idiomatic line; means raise/keep alive.

proposals.before: Meng Chang Jun house industry thick treat them, with reason incline world scholars.
proposals.after: Mengchang Jun set aside his estate and treated them generously; for this reason he drew the scholars of the world.
proposals.reason: 舍業 refers to setting aside household resources for lodging and support, not the unnatural calque 'house industry'.

proposals.before: When Lord Mengchang arrived, King Min made him chancellor of Qi and entrusted government to him.
proposals.after: When Lord Mengchang arrived, he was made chancellor of Qi and entrusted with the government.
proposals.reason: The Chinese leaves the appointer subject silent; inserting King Min is interpretive continuation rather than source wording.

proposals.before: Meng Chang Jun angry retire Wei Zi.
proposals.after: Meng Chang Jun angry and dismiss Wei Zi.
proposals.reason: 『退』 means dismiss or send away the retainer; English 'retire' wrongly suggests voluntary retirement.

proposals.before: Meng Chang Jun because thank illness, return old at Xue.
proposals.after: Meng Chang Jun because plead illness, return to old age at Xue.
proposals.reason: 『謝病』 means to decline on grounds of illness ('plead illness'), not to thank illness.

proposals.before: Su Dai then said to Lord Mengchang: 'Zhou Zui has been deeply attached to Qi, yet the King of Qi expelled him. If he listens to Qin Fu and does not make Lu Li chancellor, it is because he wishes to win over Qin.
proposals.after: Su Dai then said to Lord Mengchang: 'Zhou Zui has been deeply attached to Qi, yet the King of Qi expelled him and listened to Qin Fu while making Lu Li chancellor, because he wished to win over Qin.
proposals.reason: Chinese 聽親弗相呂禮 has no negation; the king listens to Qin Fu and makes Lu Li chancellor in order to win Qin, so the inserted English 'does not' reverses the sense.

proposals.before: Marquis Rang then spoke to King Zhao of Qin about attacking Qi, and Lü Li perished.
proposals.after: Marquis Rang then spoke to King Zhao of Qin about attacking Qi, and Lü Li fled.
proposals.reason: In this political sequel 亡 means fled into exile, matching the literal and the narrative of Lü Li losing position after the attack counsel, not that he died.

proposals.before: Answer: Feng mister very poor, still have one sword, moreover sing song.
proposals.after: Answer: Feng mister very poor, still have one sword, moreover rush-wrapped hilt.
proposals.reason: 蒯緱 is the rush wrapping on the sword hilt, not 'sing song'; the idiomatic already has the correct sense.

proposals.before: The guest house manager said: 'The guest in the upper quarters, Master Feng, has a dignified appearance and manner, is an elder, and has no other special skills. He would be suitable for collecting debts.'
proposals.after: The guest house manager said: 'The guest in the upper quarters, Master Feng, has an appearance and manner that are very eloquent, is an elder, and has no other special skills. He would be suitable for collecting debts.'
proposals.reason: 甚辯 means highly eloquent or articulate in speech, not merely dignified appearance.

proposals.before: Guest house long say: Upper house guest Feng Gong appearance manner very argue, elder, no other skill ability, suitable can make collect debt.
proposals.after: Guest house long say: Upper house guest Feng Gong appearance manner very eloquent, elder, no other skill ability, suitable can make collect debt.
proposals.reason: 辯 here is eloquent/articulate; 'very argue' is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: Leave go, arrive Xue, summon take Meng Chang Jun money all meet, obtain interest money ten thousand.
proposals.after: Leave go, arrive Xue, summon take Meng Chang Jun money all meet, obtain interest money one hundred thousand.
proposals.reason: 十萬 is one hundred thousand, not ten thousand; idiomatic already has the correct figure.

proposals.before: Various ruler strong eat drink.
proposals.after: Gentlemen strongly eat drink.
proposals.reason: 諸君 is address to the assembled men (gentlemen/you all), not 'various ruler'.

proposals.before: Have jun like this, how can negative!"
proposals.after: Have jun like this, how can betray!
proposals.reason: 負 here means betray/fail in duty, not the English word 'negative'.

proposals.before: Ask its reason, say: Meng Chang Jun recruit attract world bear knight, evil person enter Xue among cover six thousand more families.
proposals.after: Ask its reason, say: Meng Chang Jun recruit attract world bear knight, evil person enter Xue among cover sixty thousand more families.
proposals.reason: Chinese 六萬餘家 means more than sixty thousand households; the literal English wrongly renders 六萬 as six thousand.

proposals.before: Lord urgent made messenger load currency secret welcome Meng Chang Lord, did not could lose time.
proposals.after: Lord urgently make messenger load gifts secretly welcome Meng Chang Lord; must not lose the timing.
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical (did not could) and obscures 不可失時也 as the warning not to miss the opportunity.

proposals.before: Qi King confused at Qin Chu slander, consider Meng Chang Jun name high his lord monopolize Qi country power, then waste Meng Chang Jun.
proposals.after: Qi King confused at Qin Chu slander, consider Meng Chang Jun name high his lord monopolize Qi country power, then depose Meng Chang Jun.
proposals.reason: 廢 here means depose/dismiss from office; rendering it as waste is a clear semantic error.

proposals.before: Ever since the King of Qi had disgraced and dismissed Lord Mengchang, his many retainers had all abandoned him.
proposals.after: Ever since the King of Qi had slandered and dismissed Lord Mengchang, his many retainers had all abandoned him.
proposals.reason: 毀廢 pairs slander (毀) with dismissal (廢); disgraced weakens the chapter link to the Qin-Chu slander that caused the deposition.

decisions.reason: 田嬰者，齊威王少子而齊宣王庶弟也：少子 is youngest son and 庶弟 is younger paternal half-brother; “concubine brother” is a mistranslation, and the proposed literal restores both kinship terms accurately.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 齊威王少子而齊宣王庶弟

decisions.reason: 其母竊舉生之 follows 勿舉也 and means she secretly raised him so that he lived; “give birth” is wrong because the birth is already stated in s0021, and the proposed literal fixes both sense and grammar.
In 吾令若去此子，而敢生之, 生之 continues the 舉/勿舉 raise-or-abandon frame after the child has already been born and grown (及長); “give birth” invents a second birth, and “raise him” matches the Chinese.
The same 敢生之 in the literal field wrongly says “give birth”; in this 舉/去此子 context it means keep alive/raise, and the proposed literal corrects that sense.
孟嘗君舍業厚遇之：舍業 means setting aside household resources for the guests, not the calque “house industry”; the proposed literal restores that sense and 以故傾天下之士.

孟嘗君至，則以為齊相 has a silent appointer, but s0092 already names King Min as the actor who had sent him away; naming King Min as the appointing subject in idiomatic English is accurate contextual rendering, not an invented agent, so removing him is only stylistic.
孟嘗君怒而退魏子：退 here is to dismiss/send away the retainer; English “retire” wrongly suggests Wei Zi’s voluntary retirement.
孟嘗君因謝病，歸老於薛：謝病 means plead illness / decline on grounds of illness, not “thank illness”; the proposed literal corrects that clear mistranslation.

聽親弗相呂禮者，欲取秦也 has no negation, and s0118 already states 呂禮相齊; the original “does not make Lu Li chancellor” reverses the Chinese, while the proposed idiomatic restores listening to Qin Fu and appointing Lu Li in order to win Qin.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 聽親弗相呂禮者，欲取秦也

decisions.reason: 而呂禮亡 in this sequel to the counsel against Lu Li’s influence means he fled/went into exile, matching the unit’s literal “fled”; “perished” wrongly treats 亡 as death.
又蒯緱 names the sword’s rush-wrapped hilt, not singing; “sing song” invents content absent from 蒯緱, and the proposed literal matches the idiomatic sense.

decisions.after: The guest house manager said: 'Master Feng, the guest in the upper quarters, is highly articulate and a man of mature years. He has no other special skills, but he should be suitable for collecting debts.'
decisions.reason: 甚辯 describes Feng as highly articulate. The revised sentence preserves that assessment without the nonsensical phrase 'an appearance and manner of great eloquence.'
甚辯 in the literal calque was rendered “very argue”; 辯 here means eloquent/articulate, and “very eloquent” corrects that mistranslation without changing the rest of the literal line.
得息錢十萬 is one hundred thousand in interest money, not ten thousand; the proposed literal restores the numeral already correct in the idiomatic.
諸君彊飲食 addresses the assembled men as “gentlemen/you all,” not “various ruler”; the proposed literal corrects that naming error.
豈可負哉：負 means betray/fail in duty toward the lord, not English “negative”; the proposed literal restores the correct verb.
蓋六萬餘家 means more than sixty thousand households; rendering 六萬 as “six thousand” is a numeral error, and the proposed literal matches the idiomatic figure.
不可失時也 is a warning not to miss the opportunity, and 載幣 are gifts; the original “did not could lose time” is ungrammatical and obscures that sense, while the proposed literal restores both.
遂廢孟嘗君：廢 means depose/dismiss from office, not “waste”; the proposed literal corrects that clear semantic error.

自齊王毀廢孟嘗君：with the king as agent, 毀廢 means he ruined/disgraced and dismissed Mengchang; “disgraced and dismissed” is accurate enough. Changing to “slandered” is stylistic and would wrongly make the king the speaker of the Qin-Chu 毀 in s0193.

claimRevisions.reason: Revised r0012 identifies the durable skill as eloquence without turning appearance and manner into a supposed skill.
